title: The absolute value of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ extends uniquely to a finite extension
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime number, $\mathbf Q_\ell$ the field of $\ell$-adic numbers with its absolute value $|\cdot|_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] with $E$ finite-dimensional as a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space, of degree $d=[E:\mathbf Q_\ell]=\dim_{\mathbf Q_\ell}E$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Then there is exactly one absolute value $|\cdot|_E:E\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ (that is: $|x|_E=0$ iff $x=0$, $|xy|_E=|x|_E|y|_E$, $|x+y|_E\leq|x|_E+|y|_E$) whose restriction to $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is $|\cdot|_\ell$, i.e. $|a|_E=|a|_\ell$ for $a\in\mathbf Q_\ell$. It is nonarchimedean: $|x+y|_E\leq\max(|x|_E,|y|_E)$ for all $x,y\in E$.
